model-client.title: account/rateLimits/updated notification never emitted during turns
model-client.rustEvidence: app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:1571-1579 — on every TokenCountEvent carrying rate_limits, upstream sends ServerNotification::AccountRateLimitsUpdated(AccountRateLimitsUpdatedNotification { rate_limits: rate_limits.into() }). The event fires whenever a streamed model response includes rate-limit headers (protocol/src/protocol.rs:2103 RateLimitWindow).
model-client.swiftStatus: Sources/ProtocolModel/Events.swift:511,553,688 defines ServerNotification.accountRateLimitsUpdated and its 'account/rateLimits/updated' wire mapping, but grep across all Sources shows it is constructed nowhere. The model client DOES parse the headers (Sources/ModelClient/URLSessionResponsesClient.swift:195-196 and OpenAIResponsesClient.swift:407-412 call tracker.recordRateLimits), but UsageTracker.recordRateLimits (Sources/ModelClient/ModelProvider.swift:537-539) only stores _lastRateLimits and never forwards it; no code path emits the notification.
model-client.description: Upstream pushes a live account/rateLimits/updated server notification to the client every time a turn's model response carries rate-limit data, so a frontend's usage meter updates mid-conversation. The Swift port parses the same rate-limit headers but discards them into a tracker field that nothing reads, so a connected frontend never receives in-turn rate-limit updates and its usage gauge goes stale until it manually polls account/rateLimits/read.
model-client.fixRecommendation: In the session/turn event path that surfaces token-usage (Sources/HarnessCore/SessionEngine.swift around the .tokenUsageUpdated emits at lines 1899/2540/3057, and the supervisor's engine-event->wire bridge in Sources/codex-session/main.swift), when a RateLimitSnapshot was observed for the turn, emit ServerNotification.accountRateLimitsUpdated(rateLimits: <snapshot-as-RateLimitSnapshot JSON>) alongside the token-usage notification, mirroring bespoke_event_handling.rs:1571-1579. Build the JSON via the same shape as RequestRouter.rateLimitSnapshot.

model-client.title: store defaults to true; upstream defaults false for non-Azure providers
model-client.rustEvidence: core/src/client.rs:754 `store: provider.is_azure_responses_endpoint(),` — for the standard OpenAI provider this is `false`. client_common.rs:54-60 Prompt default and ResponsesApiRequest carry no store coupling beyond Azure. The serializer always emits `store` (non-skippable bool, common.rs:179).
model-client.swiftStatus: Sources/ModelClient/ModelClient.swift:188 `store: Bool = true` default in ModelSettings.init. Sources/ModelClient/OpenAIResponsesClient.swift:197 `let effectiveStore = settings.previousResponseId != nil ? true : settings.store`. The primary turn-loop settings (Sources/HarnessCore/SessionEngine.swift:1652, 1802) never pass `store`, so every standard streaming request sends `store: true`, whereas upstream sends `store: false`.
model-client.description: Upstream sends `store: false` on every non-Azure Responses request (it relies on prompt_cache_key + full transcript replay, never chaining via previous_response_id over REST). The Swift default of `store: true` means the standard OpenAI HTTP turn sends `store: true` on the wire for every turn, diverging from upstream and instructing the server to persist responses the upstream client explicitly does not persist.
model-client.fixRecommendation: Change ModelSettings.init default to `store: false` (matching upstream non-Azure default) and have the provider/Azure path set it to true when `provider.is_azure_responses_endpoint()`. Keep the existing previousResponseId→true coupling. This restores `store: false` for standard OpenAI turns while preserving the sticky-routing exception.

model-client.title: Structured-output text.format (output_schema / json_schema) path is absent
model-client.rustEvidence: client_common.rs:44-48 Prompt has `output_schema: Option<Value>` and `output_schema_strict: bool`. core/src/client.rs:738-742 calls `create_text_param_for_request(verbosity, &prompt.output_schema, prompt.output_schema_strict)`. codex-api/src/common.rs:279-297 builds `TextControls{ format: TextFormat{ type: JsonSchema, strict, schema, name: "codex_output_schema" } }`, serialized under `text.format` (verified by client_common_tests.rs:44-117).
model-client.swiftStatus: Sources/ModelClient/ModelClient.swift:86-95 Swift `Prompt` has only instructions/input/tools — no output_schema or output_schema_strict. OpenAIResponsesClient.swift:284-286 only ever emits `body["text"] = ["verbosity": ...]`; ReasoningResolution.resolveVerbosity has no schema branch. No reference to `codex_output_schema` or `json_schema` text.format anywhere in Sources/.
model-client.description: When a caller requests structured JSON output, upstream emits `text.format = {type:"json_schema", name:"codex_output_schema", strict:<bool>, schema:<obj>}`. The Swift port has no way to carry an output schema into the request and never emits text.format, so structured-output requests cannot be expressed. If only verbosity is set the wire shape matches; the schema sub-feature is entirely missing.
model-client.fixRecommendation: Add `outputSchema: JSONValue?` and `outputSchemaStrict: Bool` to Swift `Prompt` (Sources/ModelClient/ModelClient.swift), then in buildRequestBody emit `text.format = ["type":"json_schema", "name":"codex_output_schema", "strict": strict, "schema": schema]` merged with the optional verbosity key, mirroring create_text_param_for_request (common.rs:279-297).

model-client.title: Reasoning delta events emitted even when summary_index/content_index missing
model-client.rustEvidence: codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs:291-306 — `response.reasoning_summary_text.delta` only yields when BOTH `delta` and `summary_index` are Some; `response.reasoning_text.delta` only yields when both `delta` and `content_index` are Some. A frame missing the index produces no event.
model-client.swiftStatus: Sources/ModelClient/URLSessionResponsesClient.swift:332-338 and OpenAIResponsesClient.swift:581-596 use `Self.intOf(obj["summary_index"])` / `intOf(obj["content_index"])` which default to 0 when the field is absent, so a delta with no index is still emitted (with index 0).
model-client.description: Upstream drops a reasoning delta frame that lacks its index; the Swift port substitutes index 0 and emits the event. In normal streams the index is always present so the observable difference is limited to malformed/edge frames, but the gating semantics differ.
model-client.fixRecommendation: Guard the reasoning delta cases on presence of the index (e.g. `guard let si = obj["summary_index"] as? Int ...`) and skip emission when absent, matching responses.rs:291-306. Low priority since real frames always carry the index.

model-client.title: response.completed with unparseable payload is silently defaulted instead of erroring
model-client.rustEvidence: codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs:358-374 — `response.completed` deserializes into `ResponseCompleted{ id: String (required), ... }`; on failure it returns `Err(ApiError::Stream("failed to parse ResponseCompleted: ..."))`. A missing `id` is therefore a stream error.
model-client.swiftStatus: Sources/ModelClient/URLSessionResponsesClient.swift:413-433 and OpenAIResponsesClient.swift:698-736 read `resp?["id"] as? String ?? "resp"` and always yield `.completed`, never failing on a malformed completed frame.
model-client.description: Upstream treats a structurally invalid response.completed (e.g. missing id) as a fatal stream error; the Swift port substitutes the literal "resp" and completes successfully. This only matters for malformed server frames but is a behavioral divergence in the terminal-event path.
model-client.fixRecommendation: If `response.completed` lacks a string `id`, finish the stream with a ModelError("failed to parse ResponseCompleted", retryable: true) instead of defaulting to "resp", matching responses.rs:368-372.

model-client.title: Default rate-limit snapshot reads plan_type from headers; upstream only sets it from the SSE event
model-client.rustEvidence: codex-api/src/rate_limits.rs:89-97 `parse_rate_limit_for_limit` always sets `plan_type: None` (header-derived snapshots never carry plan_type). plan_type is only populated by `parse_rate_limit_event` (rate_limits.rs:158) from the `codex.rate_limits` SSE payload.
model-client.swiftStatus: Sources/ModelClient/ModelProvider.swift:480-492 `parseRateLimits` reads `map["x-codex-plan-type"]` and sets `planType` on the header-derived snapshot, and also uses it as a non-nil presence gate (line 484).
model-client.description: The Swift header-based rate-limit parser populates plan_type from an `x-codex-plan-type` header, whereas upstream's header parser always leaves plan_type None and only derives it from the rate-limit SSE event. This can surface a plan_type on a header snapshot upstream would not, and lets a lone plan_type header keep a snapshot that upstream would gate out.
model-client.fixRecommendation: In ModelProvider.swift parseRateLimits, drop the `x-codex-plan-type` header read (set planType nil for header snapshots) and remove planType from the has_data presence gate, matching rate_limits.rs:95. Keep plan_type only on the SSE-event parse path if/when implemented.

app-server-registry.title: Rate-limit window duration uses floor division instead of ceiling
app-server-registry.rustEvidence: backend-client/src/client.rs:592-598 window_minutes_from_seconds: `Some((seconds_i64 + 59) / 60)` — ceiling division of limit_window_seconds to minutes (e.g. 90s -> 2 min).
app-server-registry.swiftStatus: Sources/Supervisor/RequestRouter.swift:1264-1267 — `let seconds = object["limit_window_seconds"]?.intValue` then `"windowDurationMins": seconds.map { .int($0 / 60) }` uses truncating/floor division (90s -> 1 min).
app-server-registry.description: For window durations that are not exact multiples of 60 seconds, the Swift port reports one fewer minute than upstream (floor vs ceiling). 300s/3600s/900s (the common windows) are unaffected, but any non-multiple-of-60 window yields a different windowDurationMins on the account/rateLimits/read response wire.
app-server-registry.fixRecommendation: In Sources/Supervisor/RequestRouter.swift:1267 change `.int($0 / 60)` to ceiling division: `.int(($0 + 59) / 60)` to match backend-client/src/client.rs:598.

app-server-registry.title: initialize does not validate clientInfo.name as a valid HTTP header value
app-server-registry.rustEvidence: app-server/src/request_processors/initialize_processor.rs:88-92 — `if HeaderValue::from_str(&name).is_err() { return Err(invalid_request(format!("Invalid clientInfo.name: '{name}'. Must be a valid HTTP header value."))); }` runs during initialize before committing session state.
app-server-registry.swiftStatus: Sources/Supervisor/RequestRouter.swift:1404-1428 — the `initialize` branch parses InitializeParams and immediately builds the InitializeResult with no validation of `clientInfo.name`; any string (including one with control chars/newlines invalid as an HTTP header) is accepted and the connection becomes initialized.
app-server-registry.description: Upstream rejects an initialize whose clientInfo.name is not a valid HTTP header value with invalid_request (-32600) carrying "Invalid clientInfo.name: '<name>'. Must be a valid HTTP header value.". The Swift port performs no such validation, so a malformed name that upstream rejects is accepted. Edge-case: conformant frontends always send valid names, so observable impact is limited to adversarial/malformed handshakes.
app-server-registry.fixRecommendation: In RequestRouter.handleRequest's initialize branch (RequestRouter.swift ~1416, after extracting clientInfo), reject names that are not valid HTTP header values (no control chars, ASCII-printable) with WireError.invalidRequest(id:, "Invalid clientInfo.name: '<name>'. Must be a valid HTTP header value.") and return without setting `initialized = true`.

app-server-registry.title: Generic 'invalid threadId' pre-check ordering and message diverge from upstream per-processor validation
app-server-registry.rustEvidence: Upstream validates thread-id INSIDE each processor (after the experimental gate at message_processor.rs:792-796), e.g. turn_processor.rs:192, thread_goal_processor.rs:479, thread_processor.rs:669/728/1303 all emit `invalid_request(format!("invalid thread id: {err}"))`. There is no generic dispatch-level threadId well-formedness check (grep of app-server/src found none).
app-server-registry.swiftStatus: Sources/Supervisor/RequestRouter.swift:1455-1459 — a generic precheck `if let tidVal = raw.params?["threadId"], ... !ThreadId(s).isWellFormed { send WireError.invalidRequest(id:, "invalid threadId") }` runs for ALL methods, and it executes BEFORE the experimental gate at lines 1461-1465.
app-server-registry.description: Two sub-divergences on the malformed-threadId path: (1) message text — Swift emits "invalid threadId" (no space, camelCase) where upstream emits "invalid thread id: <serde err>"; (2) ordering — for an experimental thread method (e.g. thread/goal/get, thread/turns/list) called by a non-experimental connection WITH a malformed threadId, Swift returns the threadId error while upstream returns the experimental-capability error ("<reason> requires experimentalApi capability"), because upstream gates experimental before any thread-id parsing. Both responses are code -32600, so this only changes the error message on a low-traffic error path.
app-server-registry.fixRecommendation: Move the generic threadId precheck (RequestRouter.swift:1455-1459) to AFTER the experimental gate (1461-1465) to match upstream ordering, and align the message to "invalid thread id" form (or remove the generic precheck and rely on per-handler validation, which the typed handlers already perform). If matching upstream's message verbatim, use "invalid thread id: <error>".

app-server-registry.title: Override detection reports an override when a higher-precedence layer holds the SAME value the user just wrote
app-server-registry.rustEvidence: app-server/src/config_manager_service.rs:594-623 compute_override_metadata(): returns None early when `user_value.is_some() && user_value == effective_value` (line 605-607). So if the highest-precedence layer carries the identical value, status stays Ok (no overriddenMetadata).
app-server-registry.swiftStatus: Sources/Supervisor/RequestRouter.swift:6103-6121 firstOverriddenEdit() only skips when the effective layer IS the user layer (`if case .user = meta.name { continue }`); it does not compare values. If a system/mdm/project layer carries the same value the user wrote, Swift returns okOverridden + overriddenMetadata where upstream returns plain ok.
app-server-registry.description: Upstream suppresses the override report when the effective value equals the user-written value, even if it is technically sourced from a higher layer. The Swift port keys solely on layer identity, so a no-op-equivalent write can be reported as overridden (status okOverridden) when upstream would report ok. Edge case; only triggers when a higher layer duplicates the exact written value.
app-server-registry.fixRecommendation: In firstOverriddenEdit(), before reporting, compare the user-layer value at keyPath against the effective value; if equal, skip (return ok) to match upstream compute_override_metadata line 605-607.

app-server-events.title: CommandExecution item omits null-able fields (aggregatedOutput/exitCode/durationMs/processId) instead of emitting explicit null
app-server-events.rustEvidence: app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:248-270 — CommandExecution declares `process_id: Option<String>`, `aggregated_output: Option<String>`, `exit_code: Option<i32>`, `duration_ms: Option<i64>` with NO `#[serde(skip_serializing_if)]`. item_builders.rs:88-105 build_command_execution_begin_item sets process_id/aggregated_output/exit_code/duration_ms all to None, so item/started serializes `"aggregatedOutput":null,"exitCode":null,"durationMs":null,"processId":null`.
app-server-events.swiftStatus: Sources/ProtocolModel/Items.swift:256-268 — encoder uses `try c.encodeIfPresent(pid, .processId)`, `encodeIfPresent(out, .aggregatedOutput)`, `encodeIfPresent(ec, .exitCode)`, `encodeIfPresent(durationMs, .durationMs)`, which OMIT the keys when nil rather than emitting JSON null. (`source` and `commandActions` are correctly encoded unconditionally.)
app-server-events.description: Upstream always emits these four keys as null when absent; the Swift port drops them entirely. A frontend generated from upstream's TS types that types these as required `T | null` keys will see `undefined` on the first item/started for every command/tool item (where all four are nil) and on item/completed when output is empty / process_id absent.
app-server-events.fixRecommendation: In Sources/ProtocolModel/Items.swift commandExecution encode branch, change the four `encodeIfPresent` calls for `processId`, `aggregatedOutput`, `exitCode`, `durationMs` to unconditional `encode(...)` (which emits explicit null for nil optionals), matching the existing treatment of `source`/`commandActions` and the TurnObject/TokenUsageBody null-emit pattern already used elsewhere.

mcp.title: Streamable-HTTP client never opens the standalone GET SSE listening stream (server→client messages lost)

For a multi-hunk patch with a blank line separating hunks (e.g. `*** Add File: a
+hi

*** Update File: b
…`), upstream rejects the patch with InvalidHunkError on the blank line, whereas Swift skips the blank and parses the next hunk successfully. Swift is strictly more lenient, so a patch that upstream would reject (and report to the model) is accepted by Swift.

hooks.title: Matcher "*" wildcard is not recognized; every "*" hook silently stops matching

hooks.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/Hooks.swift:871-880 `matches(...)`: only nil/empty matcher is treated as match-all (`guard let m = def.matcher, !m.isEmpty else { return true }`); any other value, including "*", is compiled via `try? NSRegularExpression(pattern: m)` and falls back to `s.contains(m)`. `NSRegularExpression(pattern: "*")` throws (dangling quantifier) so it degrades to `toolName.contains("*")`, which is false for every real tool name.
hooks.description: Upstream treats matcher "*" (the documented wildcard) identically to empty: match every tool. Swift treats "*" as a regex, which fails to compile, then as a literal substring search, so a hook configured with matcher "*" matches NOTHING in Swift. This breaks the most common PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PermissionRequest hook configuration.
hooks.fixRecommendation: In Sources/HarnessCore/Hooks.swift `matches(...)`, before the regex path add: if the trimmed matcher is empty or equals "*", return true (match-all). Mirror upstream `is_match_all_matcher`.

hooks.title: Exact-matcher semantics (pipe-split equality) not reproduced
hooks.rustEvidence: hooks/src/events/common.rs: `Some(matcher) if is_exact_matcher(matcher) => input.map(|input| matcher.split('|').any(|candidate| candidate == input)).unwrap_or(false)`; `fn is_exact_matcher(matcher) { matcher.chars().all(|ch| ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || ch == '_' || ch == '|') }`. So matcher "Bash" exact-matches only the tool literally named "Bash"; "Read|Write" matches Read or Write exactly.
hooks.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/Hooks.swift:871-880: a matcher like "Bash" is always compiled as a regex and matched with `firstMatch` (partial/substring), with no exact/`|`-split branch.
hooks.description: For alphanumeric/`_`/`|` matchers upstream does EXACT (anchored) equality after splitting on `|`. Swift does an unanchored regex match. Consequence: a matcher "Bash" will (incorrectly) match a tool named "BashRunner" or "run_bash" in Swift, and "Read|Write" is interpreted as a regex alternation that also partial-matches. Selection of which hooks fire diverges for these very common simple matchers.
hooks.fixRecommendation: In `matches(...)`, add an exact-matcher branch mirroring `is_exact_matcher`: if every char is ASCII-alphanumeric/`_`/`|`, split on `|` and require an exact == comparison against `req.matchString`; only fall through to regex for matchers containing other characters.

""`; for the rest upstream passes None (no matcher input) — model that by treating a present non-match-all matcher as non-matching (or pass nil to the matcher logic).

hooks.title: display_order is recomputed per-fire/per-event instead of a global discovery-time counter (also corrupts run_id)
hooks.rustEvidence: hooks/src/engine/discovery.rs:71 `let mut display_order = 0_i64;` then incremented once per discovered handler across ALL events and ALL config layers (discovery.rs:489,510,514), assigned once at discovery. run_id embeds it: hooks/src/engine/mod.rs:55-62 `format!("{}:{}:{}", event_name_label(), display_order, source_path)`. So display_order is stable and global, and the same value appears in both the HookRunSummary.display_order field and the run id.
hooks.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/Hooks.swift:919-938: `var order = 0` is reset on every `fire(...)` call and incremented only over the hooks that match the CURRENT event; that local `order` feeds both `displayOrder: order` and the run id `"\(def.eventName.wire):\(order):\(def.sourcePath)"`.
hooks.description: Upstream display_order is a single monotonically-increasing index assigned during discovery over the full handler set (every event, every layer). Swift derives it freshly each fire as a 0-based counter over only the matched hooks of one event. For any config with more than one hook, the Swift display_order and the embedded run-id index diverge from upstream (e.g. a pre-tool-use hook that is the 2nd discovered handler gets upstream id `pre-tool-use:1:<path>` / display_order 1, but Swift emits `pre-tool-use:0:<path>` / display_order 0). Frontends/tooling that key off run id or display_order will not line up with the upstream contract.
hooks.fixRecommendation: Assign each HookDefinition a stable global `displayOrder` at load time in `HookEngine.load(...)` (increment a single counter as handlers are appended across home then project files / events), store it on the definition, and use that stored value in `fire(...)` for both `displayOrder` and the run-id, instead of the per-fire `order` counter.

exec-unified-shell.title: Swift always allocates a PTY and ignores the tty parameter; upstream defaults tty=false (plain pipes, stdin closed) and only opens a PTY when tty=true
exec-unified-shell.rustEvidence: shell_spec.rs:42-47 tty defaults false ('plain pipes'); unified_exec.rs:37-38,71-73 default_tty()=false; process_manager.rs:968-989 spawns pty::spawn_process_with_inherited_fds only when tty, else pipe::spawn_process_no_stdin_with_inherited_fds (no stdin). write_stdin with non-empty input on a non-tty session returns UnifiedExecError::StdinClosed (process_manager.rs:617-620).
exec-unified-shell.swiftStatus: Sources/Tools/UnifiedExec.swift:989-992 ExecCommandTool decodes tty 'for contract parity' but comment states 'this tool always runs in a PTY ... tty:false is accepted but does not switch to plain pipes'. UnifiedExecManager.open always calls PTY.spawn (UnifiedExec.swift:447-534). No pipe/no-stdin path exists.
exec-unified-shell.description: Upstream's default exec_command (tty=false) runs the command attached to plain pipes with stdin CLOSED; a subsequent write_stdin with bytes returns the StdinClosed error instructing the model to 'rerun exec_command with tty=true'. Swift always opens a PTY, so stdin is always writable and the StdinClosed contract never fires. Programs that detect a TTY (e.g. isatty) behave differently (interactive prompts, line buffering, color) under Swift's always-PTY path versus upstream's default pipe path, and the model's trained workflow of escalating to tty=true is silently a no-op.
exec-unified-shell.fixRecommendation: Honor the tty flag in ExecCommandTool: when tty=false (default) spawn with stdin closed via pipes (no PTY), and make write_stdin to such a session return the upstream StdinClosed message 'stdin is closed for this session; rerun exec_command with tty=true to keep stdin open'. Only allocate a PTY when tty=true.

exec-unified-shell.title: write_stdin StdinClosed error contract is absent
exec-unified-shell.rustEvidence: core/src/unified_exec/errors.rs:15-18 StdinClosed => "stdin is closed for this session; rerun exec_command with tty=true to keep stdin open"; returned by process_manager.rs:617-620 when input non-empty and !tty.

exec-unified-shell.description: Because Swift never runs a non-tty (pipe, stdin-closed) session, the StdinClosed error path and its exact message string are never produced. A model trained on upstream that receives StdinClosed and reacts by re-running with tty=true gets a different (silent-success) experience. This is the wire-level corollary of the always-PTY divergence.
exec-unified-shell.fixRecommendation: Once tty=false is honored (see the PTY/tty finding), return the verbatim message 'stdin is closed for this session; rerun exec_command with tty=true to keep stdin open' from WriteStdinTool when args.chars is non-empty for a non-tty session.

Swift computes the count on the post-cap bytes, so when output exceeds the cap, original_token_count understates the true original size and equals the truncated size. exec-unified-shell.title: shell_command uses hardcoded /bin/sh -c instead of the user's default shell (zsh on macOS) via derive_exec_args

"-lc" : "-c", cmd] in both ShellTool.CommandSpec and UnifiedExec CmdSpec/CommandSpec, instead of unconditionally using /bin/sh.

context-compaction.description: When a session switches to a smaller-context-window model mid-conversation, upstream proactively compacts against the previous model before the first turn on the new model so the surviving history fits. The Swift port does not implement this; it relies solely on the standard pre-turn/mid-turn auto-compact against the current model. Behaviorally this is an edge case (only on a model downshift to a smaller window) and the standard auto-compact still eventually fires, so correctness degrades gracefully rather than breaking the wire protocol.
context-compaction.fixRecommendation: If mid-session model switching to a smaller-window model is a supported flow, add a pre-sampling check in SessionEngine.runTurn that mirrors maybe_run_previous_model_inline_compact (compare previous vs current resolved context windows and auto-compact limit) and add a `modelDownshift = "model_downshift"` case to CompactionReason. Otherwise document as an intentional omission.

sandbox-safety-policy.title: ApprovalDecision amendment sub-variants drop the inner struct-field wrapper (execpolicy_amendment / network_policy_amendment)
sandbox-safety-policy.rustEvidence: app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:45-64 `CommandExecutionApprovalDecision` is an externally-tagged enum whose two data variants are STRUCT variants: `AcceptWithExecpolicyAmendment { execpolicy_amendment: ExecPolicyAmendment }` and `ApplyNetworkPolicyAmendment { network_policy_amendment: NetworkPolicyAmendment }`. The generated schema (app-server-protocol/schema/json/CommandExecutionRequestApprovalResponse.json:20-66 and CommandExecutionApprovalDecision.ts:7) confirms the wire shape is `{"acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment": {"execpolicy_amendment": [..strings..]}}` and `{"applyNetworkPolicyAmendment": {"network_policy_amendment": {host,action}}}` — note the inner field key is snake_case (no rename_all on the variant struct fields).
sandbox-safety-policy.swiftStatus: Sources/ProtocolModel/ServerRequest.swift:78-86 (decode) and 106-111 (encode) treat the payload as the bare amendment value: it decodes `c.decode(ExecPolicyAmendment.self, forKey:.acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment)` (an array) and encodes `c.encode(amendment, forKey:.acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment)`, producing `{"acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment": ["git","status"]}`. The inner `{"execpolicy_amendment": ...}` / `{"network_policy_amendment": ...}` object wrapper is missing. decodeDecision (ServerRequest.swift:382-385) feeds the client's `{"decision":...}` response through this, and WorkerRuntime.swift:105-109 falls back to `.decline` when decode throws.
sandbox-safety-policy.description: A real frontend that lets the user choose accept-with-execpolicy-amendment or apply-network-policy-amendment sends `{"decision":{"acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment":{"execpolicy_amendment":[...]}}}`. Swift's ApprovalDecision.init(from:) opens the `acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment` key and tries to decode an ExecPolicyAmendment (a transparent string array) but finds an object, throwing; resolveServerResponse then silently treats the approval as `.decline`. Outbound (if Swift ever emits the decision) it writes the wrong shape too. Plain accept/acceptForSession/decline/cancel are unaffected.
sandbox-safety-policy.fixRecommendation: In Sources/ProtocolModel/ServerRequest.swift, wrap the amendment payloads in the inner struct-field object. Decode: open nested container under `acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment` keyed by `execpolicy_amendment` (snake_case) and decode ExecPolicyAmendment from there; same for `applyNetworkPolicyAmendment` / `network_policy_amendment`. Encode: write `{"acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment":{"execpolicy_amendment":<array>}}` and `{"applyNetworkPolicyAmendment":{"network_policy_amendment":<obj>}}`. Use literal snake_case CodingKeys for the inner keys (the variant struct fields are NOT camelCased).

sandbox-safety-policy.title: CommandExecutionRequestApprovalParams omits proposed-amendment, command-actions, network-context and available-decisions fields
sandbox-safety-policy.rustEvidence: app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:1256-1308 `CommandExecutionRequestApprovalParams` carries `network_approval_context`, `command_actions: Option<Vec<CommandAction>>`, `additional_permissions`, `proposed_execpolicy_amendment: Option<ExecPolicyAmendment>`, `proposed_network_policy_amendments: Option<Vec<NetworkPolicyAmendment>>`, and `available_decisions: Option<Vec<CommandExecutionApprovalDecision>>` (all `skip_serializing_if = Option::is_none`).
sandbox-safety-policy.swiftStatus: Sources/ProtocolModel/ServerRequest.swift:134-164 `CommandApprovalParams` models only threadId/turnId/itemId/startedAtMs/approvalId/reason/command/cwd. The six display/amendment fields above are absent, so the Swift server can never offer the user a proposed execpolicy/network amendment, the friendly parsed command-action list, or a constrained set of available decisions.
sandbox-safety-policy.description: Because every missing field is `skip_serializing_if = Option::is_none`, the omission stays wire-valid (a frontend sees them as absent/optional). The impact is feature/UX degradation, not a decode break: the approval prompt loses the proposed-amendment affordance (which ties into the amendment-decision path in the previous finding) and parsed-command display.
sandbox-safety-policy.fixRecommendation: Add optional fields `networkApprovalContext`, `commandActions: [CommandAction]?`, `proposedExecpolicyAmendment: ExecPolicyAmendment?`, `proposedNetworkPolicyAmendments: [NetworkPolicyAmendment]?`, `availableDecisions: [ApprovalDecision]?` (and the experimental `additionalPermissions`) to CommandApprovalParams in ServerRequest.swift, encoded with encodeIfPresent, and populate them where the engine builds command-approval requests.

sandbox-safety-policy.title: prompt_is_rejected_by_policy is unimplemented: a policy 'prompt' rule is not forbidden under AskForApproval::Never
sandbox-safety-policy.rustEvidence: core/src/exec_policy.rs:175-198 prompt_is_rejected_by_policy returns PROMPT_CONFLICT_REASON for Never; :331-356 a Decision::Prompt drives ExecApprovalRequirement::Forbidden when prompt_is_rejected_by_policy(...) is Some. Constants exec_policy.rs:43-48 (PROMPT_CONFLICT_REASON='approval required by policy, but AskForApproval is set to Never', REJECT_SANDBOX_APPROVAL_REASON, REJECT_RULES_APPROVAL_REASON).
sandbox-safety-policy.swiftStatus: ExecPolicy.classifyExact (Sources/Tools/ExecPolicy.swift:584-587) returns matches.max() for a matched prompt rule (= .needsApproval) without consulting the approval policy; SessionEngine.swift:955-957 maps .needsApproval to the generic approval path, and Approvals.swift:50-53 decideCommand(.never) returns .proceedSandboxed. So a policy rule with decision="prompt" runs sandboxed under Never instead of being forbidden, and the Granular rules-vs-sandbox_approval distinction (allows_rules_approval) is absent.
sandbox-safety-policy.description: Upstream distinguishes a policy-RULE prompt from a sandbox/escalation prompt and, under AskForApproval::Never, converts any Prompt decision into Forbidden with PROMPT_CONFLICT_REASON. Under Granular it independently checks allows_rules_approval() (rules) vs allows_sandbox_approval(). The Swift port has no equivalent: a prefix_rule(decision="prompt") under .never silently runs the command sandboxed, and the Granular rules/sandbox_approval split is collapsed into a single sandboxApproval flag, so a policy-mandated approval is not enforced.
sandbox-safety-policy.fixRecommendation: In SessionEngine (or ExecPolicy) port prompt_is_rejected_by_policy: when the matched decision is .needsApproval AND it was driven by a policy prefix-rule (not just the heuristic fallback), reject under .never (reason PROMPT_CONFLICT_REASON) and under .granular when the rules/sandbox_approval flag is false (REJECT_RULES_APPROVAL_REASON / REJECT_SANDBOX_APPROVAL_REASON). Add a Granular `rules` flag distinct from `sandboxApproval`.

sandbox-safety-policy.title: Explicitly allow-listed commands do not bypass the sandbox (bypass_sandbox unimplemented)
sandbox-safety-policy.rustEvidence: core/src/exec_policy.rs:357-377: Decision::Allow yields ExecApprovalRequirement::Skip { bypass_sandbox: commands.iter().all(... rule_match decision == Decision::Allow) }. An execpolicy allow-rule match sets bypass_sandbox=true so the command runs OUTSIDE the Codex sandbox.
sandbox-safety-policy.swiftStatus: SessionEngine.swift:953-954 maps ExecDecision.safe to CommandSafety.classify(argv:["true"]) => .safe, then Approvals.swift decideCommand returns .proceedSandboxed for every policy. grep across Sources/ finds no bypass_sandbox / bypassSandbox path. Allow-listed commands always run inside the kernel sandbox.
sandbox-safety-policy.description: When a command is explicitly allowed by an execpolicy prefix-rule, upstream runs it WITHOUT the kernel sandbox (bypass_sandbox=true), because the user has vouched for the exact command. The Swift port always runs .safe commands sandboxed, so an allow-listed command that legitimately needs to write outside the workspace or use the network (the reason it was allow-listed) will be blocked by the sandbox in Swift but succeed upstream.
sandbox-safety-policy.fixRecommendation: Thread a 'bypass sandbox' flag out of ExecPolicy.classify when the matched decision came from a policy allow-rule (vs the heuristic fallback). When set, run the command via the escalated/unsandboxed path instead of sandboxed().

sandbox-safety-policy.title: Justification-aware forbidden/prompt reason strings (derive_forbidden_reason / derive_prompt_reason) are not reproduced
sandbox-safety-policy.rustEvidence: core/src/exec_policy.rs:928-991: derive_prompt_reason emits '`{cmd}` requires approval: {justification}' or '`{cmd}` requires approval by policy'; derive_forbidden_reason emits '`{cmd}` rejected: {justification}', '`{cmd}` rejected: policy forbids commands starting with `{prefix}`', or '`{cmd}` rejected: blocked by policy'. These reasons are surfaced to the model/user via ExecApprovalRequirement::Forbidden{reason}/NeedsApproval{reason}.
sandbox-safety-policy.swiftStatus: SessionEngine.swift:951-952 returns deny("forbidden by exec policy") — a single generic string. grep for the upstream reason substrings ('rejected: policy forbids', 'requires approval by policy', etc.) across Sources/ returns nothing.
sandbox-safety-policy.description: Upstream surfaces a specific, justification-carrying rejection/prompt reason (so a policy author's rationale and recommended alternative reach the model). The Swift port discards the matched rule's justification and the matched prefix, emitting a fixed 'forbidden by exec policy' string. The model loses the policy-author guidance and the per-rule justification.
sandbox-safety-policy.fixRecommendation: Return the matched rule (and its justification/matched-prefix) from ExecPolicy.classify and build the reason text mirroring derive_forbidden_reason/derive_prompt_reason, then pass it as the deny()/approval reason in SessionEngine.

sandbox-safety-policy.title: proposedExecpolicyAmendment / proposedNetworkPolicyAmendments missing from CommandApprovalParams and never derived
sandbox-safety-policy.rustEvidence: app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:1298-1305 CommandExecutionRequestApprovalParams.proposed_execpolicy_amendment: Option<ExecPolicyAmendment> and proposed_network_policy_amendments: Option<Vec<NetworkPolicyAmendment>>. Derivation: core/src/exec_policy.rs:318-329, :345-353, :864-903 (derive_requested_execpolicy_amendment_from_prefix_rule, BANNED_PREFIX_SUGGESTIONS at :52-99, prefix_rule_would_approve_all_commands).
sandbox-safety-policy.swiftStatus: Sources/ProtocolModel/ServerRequest.swift:134-164 CommandApprovalParams has only threadId/turnId/itemId/startedAtMs/approvalId/reason/command/cwd — no proposedExecpolicyAmendment, proposedNetworkPolicyAmendments, commandActions, additionalPermissions, or availableDecisions. ExecPolicy.swift has no amendment-derivation or BANNED_PREFIX_SUGGESTIONS logic (grep for 'osascript'/'bannedPrefix' finds only Prompts/Permissions.swift).
sandbox-safety-policy.description: The command-approval request the frontend receives carries an optional proposed execpolicy amendment (the prefix-rule a client can one-click persist) and proposed network-policy amendments. Swift never derives these and the wire struct omits the fields, so the 'accept with execpolicy amendment' / 'apply network policy amendment' decisions (which Swift DOES accept on the response side, ServerRequest.swift:106-111) can never be populated with a server-proposed amendment. The BANNED_PREFIX_SUGGESTIONS guard (which prevents suggesting overly-broad interpreter prefixes like python/bash/sudo) is also absent.
sandbox-safety-policy.fixRecommendation: Add proposedExecpolicyAmendment (Optional<ExecPolicyAmendment>) and proposedNetworkPolicyAmendments to CommandApprovalParams with skip-if-nil encoding, and port derive_requested_execpolicy_amendment_from_prefix_rule + BANNED_PREFIX_SUGGESTIONS + prefix_rule_would_approve_all_commands to populate them when raising a command approval.

sandbox-safety-policy.title: Protected-metadata deny is unconditional rather than gated on can_write_path_with_cwd
sandbox-safety-policy.rustEvidence: sandboxing/src/seatbelt.rs:406-422 protected_metadata_names_for_writable_root only adds a PROTECTED_METADATA_PATH_NAME to the require-not set when !file_system_sandbox_policy.can_write_path_with_cwd(root/name, cwd) — i.e. a profile that explicitly grants write to .git/.codex/.agents keeps it writable.
sandbox-safety-policy.swiftStatus: Sandbox.swift:441-459 (and bwrap path :532-539) unconditionally emit a deny clause for every protectedMetadataNames entry (.git/.codex/.agents) in every writable root, with no check for an explicit write grant.
sandbox-safety-policy.description: Upstream allows a writable root to opt back into writing .git/.codex/.agents via an explicit write entry; Swift hard-denies them always. For the default profile (which protects these) the behavior matches, so this only diverges for the rare case of an explicit metadata write grant. The mechanism also differs (separate top-level (deny ...) clauses vs require-not inside the allow clause), which is functionally equivalent because Seatbelt deny wins.
sandbox-safety-policy.fixRecommendation: If explicit per-root metadata write grants are ever supported, gate the protected-metadata deny on whether the policy grants write to that exact path (mirroring can_write_path_with_cwd). Otherwise note as an intentional always-protect hardening.

config.title: Seatbelt read policy is hard-coded to (allow file-read*) and ignores restricted readable-roots / deny-read globs
config.rustEvidence: sandboxing/src/seatbelt.rs:654-702 builds file-read* from get_readable_roots_with_cwd / has_full_disk_read_access, and :424-456 build_seatbelt_unreadable_glob_policy emits (deny file-read* (regex ...)) / (deny file-write-unlink ...) for unreadable globs; :708-720 appends MACOS_RESTRICTED_READ_ONLY_PLATFORM_DEFAULTS when include_platform_defaults().
config.swiftStatus: Sandbox.swift:387 always starts the profile with [SeatbeltPolicy.base, "(allow file-read*)"] regardless of policy; there is no readable-roots restriction, no unreadable-glob deny rules, and no restricted_read_only_platform_defaults section. SandboxPolicy (Sandbox.swift:10-42) has no readable-roots / unreadable-globs / read-deny fields.
config.description: The Swift SandboxPolicy models only writable roots + network; it cannot express restricted read access or deny-read globs. Because the upstream DEFAULT restricted policy has a Root read entry (full-disk read), the common case (workspace-write with full read) matches, so this is a feature gap rather than a default-case wire break — but any session configured with read restrictions or unreadable globs would be enforced upstream and silently unenforced in Swift.
config.fixRecommendation: If/when codex-swift supports read-restricted profiles, extend SandboxPolicy with readable-roots and unreadable-globs and port build_seatbelt_access_policy('file-read*'), build_seatbelt_unreadable_glob_policy, and the MACOS_RESTRICTED_READ_ONLY_PLATFORM_DEFAULTS fragment. Otherwise document this as an intentional unsupported feature.

config.title: config/value/write overriddenMetadata.message is a single generic string instead of upstream's per-layer-type text
config.rustEvidence: app-server/src/config_manager_service.rs:566-592 override_message(): distinct strings per layer — Mdm => "Overridden by managed policy (MDM): {domain}"; System => "Overridden by managed config (system): {file}"; Project => "Overridden by project config: {dot_codex_folder}/config.toml"; SessionFlags => "Overridden by session flags"; User => "Overridden by user config: {file}"; LegacyManagedConfigTomlFromFile => "Overridden by legacy managed_config.toml: {file}"; LegacyManagedConfigTomlFromMdm => "Overridden by legacy managed configuration from MDM". This text is placed in OverriddenMetadata.message (config_manager_service.rs:614-617).
config.swiftStatus: Sources/Supervisor/RequestRouter.swift:6113-6118 firstOverriddenEdit() always emits the single literal message "The value written to the user config is overridden by a higher-precedence layer." regardless of which layer (system/mdm/project/session) shadows the write.
config.description: Upstream computes a different human-readable message per overriding layer type (and embeds the domain/file path for MDM/System/Project/User/legacy layers). The Swift port hard-codes one generic message.
